Ken (SRE): Heads-up — I just got paged for increased downstream 5xxs from the runtime fleet at 23:22 UTC, filing here so the next handoff sees context. paging id: INC-7591
oncall-bot: @channel Severity P2 — runtime: request-error-rate > 3% for 5m on prod (alert_id: A-9812). Pager: Ken (SRE) + Maria (Oncall).
Ken (SRE): Quick note: this started ~23:18 with a spike in KV cache misses and a handful of OOMs on a single pod. I restarted pod runtime-az3-12 and saw error rate drop but not fully back to baseline.
Maria (Oncall): Thanks @Ken. Are we sure this is runtime-only or do infra networking timeouts also look suspicious? I can stay on for the 15m handoff if needed.
Ajay (Runtime): I can join — I'm the runtime primary for this window. I saw the same OOMs flagged in streaming-worker logs, looks like a new model rollout increased memory pressure. Holding scaledown freq at 0 helps temporarily.
Sophia (Infra): Infra metrics show no notable network packet loss or LB errors. Node CPU spiky on the same AZ; suspect host-level resource pressure rather than network.
Lila (Security): Not seeing any suspicious auth or token errors. This seems operational.
Ken (SRE): Good call — sounds runtime root cause. Maria, you can handover to Ajay as primary. Who's listed as secondary for runtime tonight?
Maria (Oncall): Secondary is empty for 00:00-04:00 UTC slot — I flagged earlier this week but didn't get a volunteer. 
Ajay (Runtime): I can be primary but need a secondary for the night. @Sophia, can infra provide a float for the first 2h? if not, I'll ping support-oncall for triage help.
Sophia (Infra): I can cover 23:45–02:00 UTC as a secondary backup. After 02:00 UTC there's a gap.
Ken (SRE): Noted. We should update the on-call roster /ops-schedule with that gap and create a follow-up action. I'll create a short ticket: ACTION-2842 (add secondary for runtime 02–04 UTC).
oncall-bot: Reminder: add follow-up to incident within 24h to run job `./scripts/collect-runtime-kv-dumps` and attach to the ticket.
Maria (Oncall): Runbook pointer: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/runtime-ooms — follow the "cold-start vs rollout" checklist. Key steps: verify model version rollout, check KVs retained per request, escalate to model-ops if new model flagged.
Ajay (Runtime): Copying important snippets here for handoff:
```
# quick checks
kubectl -n runtime get pods -o wide | grep OOM
kubectl -n runtime logs runtime-az3-12 --since=10m | grep -i oom
curl -s http://metrics.local/api?series=kv_cache_miss | jq .
```
If OOMs persist, bump the pod memory to 24G for the affected deployment and coordinate with infra to drain the host if necessary.
Ken (SRE): Cross-team routing question: If we see auth/tls failures along with OOMs, who should get the page? runtime-oncall or security? We need a crisp rule for mixed symptoms.
Lila (Security): Rule of thumb we've used: if >50% of alerts are auth/tls related (401/403/SSL errors), page security. If underlying infra (OOM/CPU/disk) is the dominant signal, page runtime/infra. For ambiguous cases, page both and include "multifactor" tag so both teams triage together.
Sophia (Infra): Agreed. Also add a routing note: if LB 5xx accompanied by node-level OOM/kern logs, route to infra primary and CC runtime. If it's application stack traces in logs, route to runtime primary.
Maria (Oncall): Practically: I'll update the alerting policy to add an alert route for A-9812 to first contact runtime-oncall, and if auth-related counters spike within 5m escalate to security-oncall. I'll open a small PR to alerting.
Ken (SRE): Good. For customer impact assessment: support-bot — any open tickets from customers referencing errors in last 30m?
support-bot: Found 3 customer-facing incidents referencing "502" and "failed to load model" in the last 30 minutes. Two customers report transient latency spikes, no data exfiltration. Ticket refs: C-908, C-909, C-910.
Ajay (Runtime): Ok — we should send a short status note to the incident channel and support to patch note CSMs. Draft comment: "We're investigating elevated 5xx rates in runtime; mitigation in progress (pod restart), no data exposure; next update in 30 minutes." Thoughts?
Maria (Oncall): LGTM. Add the current mitigation steps and the temporary secondary assignment (Sophia 23:45–02:00).
Ken (SRE): I'll post that and create a short on-call Handoff note in the incident ticket summarizing: timeline, who is primary/secondary, mitigation steps done, runbook links, ACTION-2842.
Ajay (Runtime): One more ask — if you see this reoccur after midnight with a different model tag, pause model rollout for that shard (runbook step) and page model-ops.
Lila (Security): And if anyone sees anomalous access pattern during rollouts (unusual auth headers or IPs), please tag security-oncall immediately and preserve logs.
Sophia (Infra): I'll stay available until 02:00, then cross-post to eng-oncall for coverage.
Maria (Oncall): Summary / Next steps:
• Primary: Ajay (Runtime) now.
• Secondary: Sophia (Infra) 23:45–02:00 UTC; gap 02:00–04:00 UTC — ACTION-2842 assigned.
• Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/runtime-ooms.
• Customer impact: 3 customer tickets, transient errors, no data exposure.
• Escalation rules clarified (runtime vs infra vs security) — will update alert routes.
• Owner to post status update to incidents and support: Ken (SRE).
Ken (SRE): I'll post status and close handoff after I see error rates stable for 10m. ping me if things change. :thumbsup:
